## Summary

Define Value Format

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
CFEL / Format
```

### Prose Claim


Format defines the admissible value domain of each direct Property value,
separately from its cardinality. In CFEL, `Format` is the language element for
expressing that value domain. Data Type names the value domain. Uniqueness
Selection names the comparison population. List and map are Carrier
structures, not Value Formats. A YAML sequence carries multiple values, and a
mapping carries dependent Properties. `ref` is not a Value Format. Identifying
values use the `string` Format; their Definition identifies the referenced
object. Nested Properties have independent Formats and cardinalities. A Model object kind referenced as `<Kind>` may also supply an object Format alongside primitive Formats such as `int`; a Format specifies the admissible domain and does not create an instance or turn a literal into a Node. `[<Workflow Run> OR <Step Run>]` admits either declared Model kind as one union domain; a participant selected from it is one binding. Bracketed Format conditions constrain values in that domain. In `p{::occ} :: [<Kind>]{::valuecount}`, the bounds count Property occurrences and direct values respectively, not every instance of Kind in the Project. YAML
null and an empty string each count as one direct value when present; Format
and prose conditions determine admissibility.



## Semantics

Format annotations constrain direct values. Markdown, YAML, TOML and JSON are
Carrier representation formats, not value Formats. The initial scalar
vocabulary—bool, datetime, decimal, float, int and string—is provisional. A
format annotation selects a value domain; it does not impose uniqueness.

## Summary

Define Value Format

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
CFEL / Format
```

### Prose Claim

Square brackets enclose a Format and any conditions. After a Property they restrict its direct-value domain: `[int]` selects the integer Format and `[int, 0..100]` restricts it to that inclusive range. In `p.*[name format]` and `p.**[name format]`, the Format constrains selected immediate and recursive dependent Property names, respectively; those name counts remain separate from direct-value counts. Multiple conditions apply together as AND; parentheses specify the grouping of mixed conditions. A Model kind referenced through `<Kind>` can supply an object Format, and OR can combine Model-kind domains under the separate Model-kind Format rule. A Format constrains each direct Property value separately from Property occurrence and value cardinality; it does not create an instance or turn a literal into a Node.

Data Type names a value domain. Uniqueness Selection names the comparison population. List and map are Carrier structures, not Value Formats. A YAML sequence carries multiple values, and a mapping carries dependent Properties. `ref` is not a Value Format. Identifying values use the `string` Format; their Definition identifies the referenced object. Nested Properties have independent Formats and cardinalities. YAML null and an empty string each count as one direct value when present; Format and applicable conditions determine admissibility.

In `p{::occ} :: [<Kind>]{::valuecount}`, the bounds count Property occurrences and direct values respectively, not every instance of Kind in the Project.

## Semantics

A Format describes the admissible values. Markdown is a value Format for Markdown content; a Format does not impose uniqueness.

## Summary

Reference a Model entity in a CFEL Format

## Claim

### Prose Claim

`<x>` refers to the declared Model entity `x`. When used as `[<x>]`, it supplies the Format domain of existing instances of that entity, including its narrower kinds where applicable. It does not create a Model entity, an instance, or a literal value. Model Properties may supply such a domain when their instances are admitted.

A fixed Model Relation name such as `Relation//IS_CONTAINED_BY` is a Model reference and does not introduce a `$` participant. A typed participant such as `$a[<Atom>]` binds an existing instance. A Claim may relate that instance to a bare Model entity only when the applicable Relation Declaration admits those endpoint domains. For a declared kind `x`, `$a[<x>] ((INSTANCE_OF)) x` illustrates such a mixed instance-to-Model relation when its endpoints are admitted.

In `$container[<Workflow Run> OR <Step Run>]`, the alternatives define one union domain for one participant. A Relation count applies to the selected union as a whole, not separately to each alternative.

The paired `<` and `>` around the Model reference are Format markers. Binary numeric `<` and `>` are comparisons governed by their respective CFEL Rules.

## Semantics

A Model reference identifies a declared Model entity for use in a Format.

## Summary

Define INSTANCE_OF

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
$host ((INSTANCE_OF)) $target;

$direct[<Relation>, (.Name = INSTANCE_OF)];
$inverse[<Relation>, (.Name = HAS_INSTANCE)];

$direct ((HAS_INVERSE)) $inverse;

$direct ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

The Host is an instance of the Target declared kind. A Property instance is borne by its data bearer and is an instance of its corresponding model Property, which remains borne by its model bearer. A Property instance has no independent Carrier; its bearer and kind Relations are distinct and may coexist.

Forward `Host ((INSTANCE_OF)) Target` and reverse `Target <((INSTANCE_OF)) Host` are views of the same Relation fact.
INSTANCE_OF relates instance of a declared kind to declared kind.

## Summary

Define INSTANCE_OF

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
$host ((INSTANCE_OF)) $target;

Relation//HAS_INSTANCE ((IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR)) Relation//INSTANCE_OF;

Relation//INSTANCE_OF ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

The Host is an instance of the Target declared Model entity. A Property instance is borne by its data bearer and is an instance of its corresponding model Property, which remains borne by its model bearer. A Property instance has no independent Carrier; its bearer and kind Relations are distinct and may coexist.

HAS_INSTANCE is the inverse alias of INSTANCE_OF. Both writings identify the same fact, with endpoints reversed; the alias does not grant an endpoint permission or add a fact.

For a declared Model entity `x`, `$a[<x>] ((INSTANCE_OF)) x` is a generic example: `$a` selects an existing instance of `x`; bare `x` denotes that Model entity. The example does not create either participant.

## Semantics

INSTANCE_OF relates an instance to its declared Model entity.
